source.title: Compressed Decentralized Proximal Stochastic Gradient Method for Nonconvex Composite Problems with Heterogeneous Data
source.authors: Yonggui Yan; Jiewei Chen; Pin-Yu Chen; Xiao-Dong Cui; Song-Tao Lu; Yangyang Xu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares held-out accuracy for neural networks trained with large and small batches at the same epoch budget. This bears on V5, though it does not measure the train–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports objective values, test accuracy and consensus errors during training. Only its own large-batch versus small-batch test-accuracy comparisons bear on the listed versions. Other optimizer and compression comparisons do not test a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study reports lower held-out accuracy for large-batch training at fixed epoch budgets in a new setting: decentralized image classification with heterogeneous data. These results bear on V5, although batch size and training method change together.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that their small-batch decentralized methods achieve good generalization and handle heterogeneous data, outperforming the tested large-batch methods and, on FixupResNet20, a momentum variance-reduction method. Compression largely preserves testing accuracy while reducing communication.
record.recipe_differences: Decentralized proximal stochastic gradient methods, compared with large-batch and other decentralized training methods; the study does not reproduce the claim versions' original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/model and method; the text describes stronger large-batch underperformance on the more complex FixupResNet20/CIFAR-10 task.

fits_no_version.finding: CDProxSGT preserves testing accuracy while reducing communication by approximately 70% for LeNet5 and 60% for FixupResNet20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Communication compression can preserve held-out accuracy in these decentralized training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: DEEPSTORM matches DProxSGT on LeNet5 but has lower testing accuracy on FixupResNet20 at the same ordinary batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum variance reduction can impair held-out performance on some neural-network workloads.

record.problems: The relevant test-accuracy values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. Comparisons change both batch size and method, and no direct train–test gap is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted. Relevant comparisons are described in text but their measured accuracy values are figure-only; per instructions, figures without text descriptions of values do not support rows. Figures 1 and 2.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning interventions.

Language models, batch-size thresholds, longer training, warmup, and controlled normalization or regularization changes. Larger learning rates are used for large batches, but their ability to remove the penalty is not separately tested.
Dropout interventions and removing dropout together with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: DProxSGT exceeds AllReduce in FixupResNet20 testing accuracy, while their LeNet5 curves are almost identical. The authors suggest AllReduce's larger effective batch as a possible explanation; this attribution is not isolated experimentally.

record.verdict_notes: The main figure comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not repeated as missing. Exact accuracy differences cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. Training objectives and consensus errors do not themselves establish V5; held-out accuracy and the authors' explicit descriptions do.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay or switching optimizers.

Large-batch penalties are compared at the same epoch count, but exact accuracy values are shown only in figures and are not reported numerically in the text. The study does not test language models, longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, or normalization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Sparse decentralized training: ProxGT-SA versus DProxSGT on LeNet5/FashionMNIST and FixupResNet20/CIFAR-10.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.1 and Figure 1; no rows were extracted. Large batches of 256 versus 8 and 512 versus 64 perform worse at 100 and 500 epochs respectively, especially on FixupResNet20; learning rate and method also differ.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports poorer accuracy for larger-batch ProxGT-SA, but the comparisons remain unverified and also change learning rates and methods.

relationships.condition: Compressed decentralized training without regularization: BEER versus CDProxSGT on both image tasks.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.2 and Figure 2; no rows were extracted. BEER has lower testing accuracy with batches 256 versus 8 and 512 versus 64 at matching epoch budgets, despite larger tuned learning rates; algorithm differences prevent isolating batch size.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports poorer accuracy for larger-batch BEER, but the comparisons remain unverified and algorithm differences prevent isolating batch size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
